review_evidence: README identifies Veil as a foundational Lean framework for specifying, executing, testing, model-checking, and proving safety properties of transition systems and distributed protocols.

The primary source includes the framework plus extensive VeilTest regression/specification files; an inspected regression defines a transition-system module, state relations, an invariant, generated specification, and a checked expected verification failure.

These regression files therefore preserve formal specifications and verification behavior rather than merely test harness plumbing; FILTER-011 bars path-only exclusion and no lossless hard filter was established.
summary: Retain Veil's transition-system framework and regression/specification corpus because the tests encode concrete formal models and verification obligations.

summary: Surveyed all 283 listed files across Examples/ (50), Veil/ (121), VeilTest/ (110), Veil.lean and lakefile.lean; all exist in the checkout. A declaration-keyword grep (Lean declarations, tactic/elab/syntax/macro, Veil DSL commands such as veil/action/invariant/relation, and # commands) found 8 files with no match; I read all 8 in full and they are import-only or near-import-only modules (Veil.lean, Veil/DSL.lean, Veil/Frontend/DSL/State.lean, Veil/Core/Tools/ModelChecker/Simulation.lean, .../Simulation/Checker.lean, Veil/Frontend/DSL/Action/DoElab.lean, Veil/Frontend/DSL/Base.lean, Veil/Core/UI/Widget/RefreshComponent.lean). Several contain namespace or meta-section commands or module docstrings, and under FILTER-007 import-only modules stay primary-eligible without a verified auxiliary delivery path, so they are retained. The rest hold Veil protocol specifications (Examples), the DSL elaborators, tactics, weakest-precondition semantics and model-checker soundness theorems (Veil/), and regression specifications with verification obligations (VeilTest). Disposition: retain all; no exclusions.
